title: Why Greylock capped its new fund at $1.5B when it says it could have raised more
slides: Why would Greylock turn down billions of investor cash?
Its new $1.5B fund is actually smaller than the last one.
Most VCs raise bigger—Greylock shrank on purpose.
LPs wanted in but Greylock capped them to stay nimble.
Ask your GP: would you limit fund size to win?
thread_text:
1. Why shrink a fund?

Greylock cut its new fund to $1.5B, down from a bigger raise, while LPs begged for entry.

2. They said no to billions.

Most VCs chase ever-larger funds. Greylock capped theirs on purpose to stay nimble.

3. LPs locked out.

Investors wanted in, but Greylock turned down their cash to avoid bloat.

4. Nimble over huge.

A smaller fund means faster decisions. Greylock bets speed beats size.

5. Ask your GP today.

Would you limit fund size to win? Pitch that question to your own general partner this week.
